title: Risk-score five vendors before contracts are signed
situation: Procurement has five vendors waiting for approval, including a payroll provider, an air-conditioning contractor and a managed IT provider that wants administrator access. Each vendor filled in a security questionnaire, and legal shared the contract clauses actually signed. We need a decision on each vendor before anyone gets access to our data or network.
your_task: Score each vendor's inherent risk from what it will touch: data sensitivity, type of access, and how critical the service is.
Reduce that score by how well the vendor's questionnaire answers show working controls, giving residual risk.
Check the contract for required clauses, such as right-to-audit, breach-notice time and uptime promises.
Decide APPROVE, APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS or REJECT, and set how often each vendor is reviewed.
why_it_matters: Many large breaches start at a supplier, not at the company itself. A vendor with administrator access and an undisclosed conflict of interest is a direct path into our network.
done_when: All 5 vendors have inherent and residual risk scores and a decision.
Every missing clause or questionnaire gap is listed as a condition.
The Identity and Access Management (IAM) team confirms no vendor account or privileged access is created for a rejected vendor (VN-3, VN-5).

glossary.Inherent risk: The risk before any controls are counted.
glossary.Residual risk: The risk left after the vendor's controls are taken into account.
glossary.SOC 2 / ISO 27001: Independent audits that show a company's security controls really work.
glossary.Right-to-audit clause: Contract wording that lets us inspect the vendor's security ourselves.
glossary.SLA (service level agreement): A contract promise about uptime and response times.
glossary.MOU vs BPA: An MOU (memorandum of understanding) states intent and is usually not binding; a BPA (business partners agreement) sets binding partner duties.

talking_point: Assessed 5 vendors on inherent and residual risk: approved 1, approved 2 with conditions, and rejected 2, including a managed IT provider seeking privileged access that had not disclosed a conflict of interest.
